signature.name: Shenyang Imperial Palace
signature.detail: The only other imperial palace complex in China besides Beijing's Forbidden City, built by the early Qing rulers and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is smaller and far less crowded, so you can see the distinctive Manchu architecture up close. Go early on a weekday; tickets are sold at the gate and a passport is needed for foreigners.

signature.name: 9.18 Historical Museum
signature.detail: A powerful, sobering museum marking the 1931 Mukden Incident that began Japan's occupation of northeast China. The exhibits are extensive and mostly in Chinese, but the scale and artifacts speak for themselves. It is free with ID, closed Mondays, and best reached by metro plus a short walk.

signature.name: Shenyang Steam Locomotive Museum
signature.detail: A specialist museum with a large collection of preserved steam locomotives, from huge freight engines to rare prototypes. It is a must for rail fans and an unusual stop for anyone curious about industrial history. Check opening days before you go, as hours can be limited, and allow an hour or two.
